hypothesis: The exact v39 route set can produce technically valid protected live lifecycles while point-in-time route, regime, execution-friction, effective-episode, and predeclared exit-policy evidence distinguishes repeatable after-cost behavior from whipsaw, profit surrender, and correlated opportunity duplication before a separately versioned $5,000 successor is authorized.
decision: Keep the authorized v39 runtime, routes, entries, position sizing, venue stops, and bound exits unchanged. Record the ETH HT short as a second cleared-cost-hurdle-then-surrendered lifecycle, but treat ETH and SPCX as members of the same still-open five-lifecycle market episode rather than independent confirmations. Preserve the three declared profit-lock policies as report-only measurements; do not install a universal trail or retune the route from this correlated discovery evidence. Continue exact route-side observation, protected-open reconciliation, regime attribution, missed-opportunity accounting, and effective-episode collection before revising the separately versioned $5,000 successor.
falsifier: The technical conclusion is invalidated by changed source identity, unreconciled lifecycle or fill accounting, missing venue protection, a non-causal regime join, or a new technical-gap identity. The no-change decision should be revised by later point-in-time route-specific outcomes showing stable after-cost improvement across non-overlapping episodes, side coverage where supported, and positive performance without the largest winner. The route-specific profit-lock hypothesis is falsified if predeclared policies underperform unchanged provider exits after realized fees, funding, measured exit friction, multiplicity disclosure, stop precedence, and correlation-aware episode accounting.
limitations: Three raw closes are not three independent observations: ETH and SPCX belong to the same five-lifecycle episode that still contains BTC, SOL, and SP500 opens.
Only the isolated SNDK episode is completed; independence is not established and open marks are excluded from resolved decisions.
SNDK and SPCX lack canonical core-regime telemetry; provider-native context cannot be relabeled with a core-asset regime after the fact.
ETH exit context opposed the short at the component level, but the frozen regime-opposition episode recorded zero qualifying opposed decisions, so it does not establish an executable regime exit.
Selecting a profit-lock policy after these correlated losses would incur discovery-sample and multiple-testing bias; all three policies remain declared measurements.
Counterfactual exits cannot reproduce an unsubmitted private order and remain sensitive to future exit slippage, fees, and funding.
No live route, position, order, stop, target, size, exit, transition, protection, or execution process changed in this revision.
